diagram_math_checks.check: Boundary, face arcs and disk selection
diagram_math_checks.details: The radius-1.3 disk has cuts p1=(-1.2,0.5), p2=(1.2,0.5), p3=(1.2,-0.5), p4=(-1.2,-0.5), since 1.2^2+0.5^2=1.3^2. They occur clockwise in that order. The dashed boundary meets the diagram only at these four cuts; its four intervening arcs lie in faces. Infinity is drawn at (0,1.8), outside D. This instantiates the m=4 selection, face-arc gluing and side-not-containing-infinity rules of the original Definition, line 47.

The p1-to-p2 strand is continuous through two vertical crossing segments x=-0.6 and x=0.6. The p3-to-p4 strand points left at y=-0.5 and has visible under-gaps at both crossings. The first over-tangent points downward and the second upward. Thus det((0,-1),(-1,0))=-1 and det((0,1),(-1,0))=+1 under def-planar-diagram-gauss-and-dowker-codes, Definition crossing-sign paragraphs. The same strand is over at both crossings, as required by def-oriented-reidemeister-moves R2; both strands retain their boundary orientations after deletion.

diagram_math_checks.details: Each panel has exactly two properly embedded strand pieces relative to four boundary points, with two crossings on the left and none on the right. No further edge or closed component lies inside D. Outside arcs p2-to-p3 and p4-to-p1 are drawn by identical translated coordinate paths in both panels, with inherited compatible orientation and no crossings. Tracing p1,p2,p3,p4,p1 gives one component. Their identity fixes each ordered boundary point and the infinity region, satisfying the original finite-comparison outside-record requirement, not merely an abstract endpoint matching.
